title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Provisions on People's Courts Actively Accepting Supervision from Litigants in Trial and Enforcement Activities
keywords_en: actively accept cases in adjudication and enforcement activities
full_text_en:
Supreme People’s Court

Notice on Issuing the Several Provisions on People’s Courts Actively Accepting Supervision from Parties in Trial and Enforcement Activities

Fa Fa [2014] No. 13

To the High People’s Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People’s Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People’s Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Several Provisions on People’s Courts Actively Accepting Supervision from Parties in Trial and Enforcement Activities are hereby issued. Please implement them earnestly in light of actual conditions.

July 15, 2014

Several Provisions on People’s Courts Actively Accepting Supervision from Parties in Trial and Enforcement Activities

For the purposes of regulating the work of people’s courts in actively accepting supervision from parties in trial and enforcement activities, and promoting impartial, efficient, clean, and civilized judicature, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Judges Law of the People’s Republic of China.

Article 1: People’s courts and their case-handling departments and personnel shall strictly observe the discipline regarding integrity in trial and enforcement activities, continuously improve judicial conduct, and actively accept supervision from the parties.

Article 2: A people’s court shall publish in places such as its litigation service hall, case-filing hall, and dispatched people’s tribunals the court’s regulations on discipline and conduct, the telephone number for receiving reports, and the website for receiving reports.

Article 3: In the case-filing and trial procedures, the people’s court shall, through appropriate means, promptly and proactively notify the parties of key milestone information, including the results of case-filing review, preservation of assets, and procedural changes.

Article 4: In the enforcement procedure, the people’s court shall, through appropriate means, promptly and proactively notify the parties of key milestone information, including the filing of enforcement, changes to or addition of persons subject to enforcement, implementation of enforcement measures, property investigation and control, property disposal, conclusion of the current enforcement proceedings, resumption of enforcement after conclusion of current enforcement proceedings, and termination of enforcement.

Article 5: Where a party needs to learn about the progress of case handling from the people’s court, the case-handling department and personnel of the people’s court shall inform the party.

Article 6: The case-handling department of the people’s court shall, when serving the relevant legal documents on case acceptance to the party, also deliver to the party an Integrity Supervision Card. A party may also, as needed, directly obtain an Integrity Supervision Card from the litigation service hall, case-filing hall, or dispatched people’s tribunal of the people’s court.

The Integrity Supervision Card shall be made in the format prescribed by the Supreme People’s Court.

Article 7: A party may, during the case-handling period or after the case is concluded, directly mail the Integrity Supervision Card filled with the party’s opinions to the discipline inspection department of the people’s court.

The discipline inspection department of the people’s court shall uniformly handle and manage the opinions on integrity supervision reflected by the parties.

Article 8: The people’s court shall, in proportion to the total number of cases handled by the court each year, randomly select a certain percentage of cases from among those concluded or enforced in the current year to conduct integrity return visits, and actively seek the parties’ evaluation opinions on whether the case-handling personnel have observed the regulations on discipline and conduct.

Article 9: In addition to randomly selecting cases for integrity return visits, the people’s court shall also conduct integrity return visits for the following cases concluded or enforced in the current year:

(1) Cases of widespread public concern;
(2) Cases in which parties have reported violations of discipline and integrity regulations;
(3) Other cases where a return visit is necessary.

Article 10: Integrity return visits may be conducted by means of interview return visits, door-to-door return visits, telephone return visits, correspondence return visits, etc. Opinions expressed by parties during the return visit shall be recorded.

Article 11: Integrity return visits shall be organized and implemented jointly by the discipline inspection department of the people’s court and the case-handling department.

Article 12: The discipline inspection department of the people’s court shall handle opinions raised by parties in the Integrity Supervision Card and during integrity return visits in the following manner:

(1) For opinions of criticism, they shall be referred to the case-handling department, which, after ascertaining the facts, may criticize and educate the person subject to supervision as appropriate;
(2) For opinions of commendation, they shall be referred to the case-handling department, which, after ascertaining the facts, may commend and reward the person subject to supervision as appropriate;
(3) For clues of disciplinary or legal violations, they shall be investigated and handled jointly with the integrity supervisor of the case-handling department;
(4) For issues concerning case-handling procedures, application of law, and fact-finding, they shall be referred to the case-handling department, the trial supervision department, or the trial management department for handling in accordance with the relevant provisions.

Article 13: After the case-handling department of the people’s court handles the opinions of criticism raised by the party, it shall provide feedback to the party on the handling situation in a timely manner.

After the discipline inspection department of the people’s court handles the clues of disciplinary or legal violations raised by the party, it shall provide feedback to the party on the handling situation in a timely manner.

Where an inaccurate report by a party causes an adverse impact on the reported person, the discipline inspection department and the case-handling department of the people’s court shall clarify the facts for the reported person through appropriate means.

Article 14: The discipline inspection department of the people’s court shall regularly sort out and analyze the opinions raised by parties in the Integrity Supervision Card and during integrity return visits, and, based on the common problems identified through such analysis, submit opinions and suggestions for further improvement of the work to the Leading Party Members’ Group of the court.

Article 15: The discipline inspection department of the people’s court shall supervise and urge the implementation of these Provisions by all departments and their personnel of the court. The political work department of the people’s court shall include the implementation of these Provisions by the departments and their personnel in the scope of assessment.

Article 16: For a people’s court that has not yet established a discipline inspection department, the political work department of the court shall assume the functions assigned to the discipline inspection department under these Provisions.

Article 17: The term “parties” as used in these Provisions includes defendants, victims, private prosecutors, plaintiffs and defendants in incidental civil actions in criminal cases; plaintiffs, defendants, and third parties in civil and administrative cases; applicants for enforcement, persons subject to enforcement, and persons other than the parties in enforcement cases.

Upon authorization by a party, defense counsel or an agent ad litem may, on behalf of the party, receive and fill in the Integrity Supervision Card or participate in an integrity return visit.

Article 18: The work of people’s courts in actively accepting supervision from parties in death penalty review cases and state compensation cases shall be governed by separate provisions.

Article 19: Each high people’s court may, in accordance with these Provisions, formulate implementation rules for the work of actively accepting supervision from parties by the court itself and the courts within its jurisdiction.

Article 20: These Provisions shall take effect from the date of issuance, and the interpretation power rests with the Supreme People’s Court.
